stop: If your lips or tongue swell or you get breathless, stop at once and see a doctor
If your throat is no better after a week, stop and see a doctor
It mustn't be swallowed. Make sure a child is old enough to spit it out
tips: Avoiding water and food for 30 minutes after rinsing keeps the medicine there longer.
When mouth ulcers are bad, using it 15 minutes before a meal makes eating much easier.

faq.q: Can I just buy it at the pharmacy?
faq.a: Yes, **it's sold at Korean pharmacies** (non-prescription). There are mouthwash and spray products. You don't need a prescription.

faq.q: How is it different from chlorhexidine?
faq.a: Chlorhexidine is **a disinfectant**, so it only stops things getting infected — it doesn't ease the pain. Benzydamine **directly reduces the feeling of pain**. If it hurts too much to eat, benzydamine is the one.

faq.q: For how many days can I use it?
faq.a: **Don't keep using it for more than 7 days** without a doctor's guidance. If it's no better after 7 days, another cause needs checking.

benzydamine.children: Age limits differ by product. Check that the child is old enough not to swallow it.

acetylcysteine.tagline: Thins sticky phlegm — a regular in clinic cold prescriptions
acetylcysteine.lead: A mucolytic that breaks the mucus chains in phlegm to thin it. In Korean clinics it's commonly given with an anti-inflammatory for colds and bronchitis, and it's also sold at pharmacies. It doesn't stop coughing — it **makes phlegm easier to cough up**, so it only makes sense if you drink plenty of water.
for: Phlegm after bronchitis or a cold
stop: Stop if breathing feels tight or you wheeze (people with asthma)
If there's blood in the phlegm or the fever continues, see a doctor
Stop and get advice if your stomach burns badly
Stop if your heart races or you get hives, face swelling or breathlessness — if you can't breathe, call 119 at once (rarely fast heartbeat or high blood pressure, very rarely anaphylaxis)
tips: For a phlegmy cough, this medicine + water suits better than a cough suppressant.
It's not an antibiotic — it doesn't kill bacteria, it only thins phlegm.

faq.q: Will it stop the cough?
faq.a: No. It thins phlegm so it's easier to cough up, so you may cough a little more for a while. If a dry cough keeps you from sleeping, there are separate cough suppressants.

faq.q: Can I buy it at a pharmacy?
faq.a: Yes, it's a non-prescription medicine in Korea. But it's one slot in the clinic cold combination, so if it's already in your prescription bag, don't buy it separately.

acetylcysteine.children: In Korea, capsules are sold **from age 6** and granules **from age 2** (age 2–5: half a sachet 3 times a day — approved directions). Not used under 2.

mosapride.tagline: A prescription medicine that gets the stomach moving — for bloating while on anti-inflammatories
mosapride.lead: A prokinetic that speeds up stomach and gut movement to reduce bloating, nausea and fullness after meals. Korean clinics often add it to prescriptions for anti-inflammatories or cold medicines **to ease stomach discomfort**. Its job is different from acid blockers such as famotidine or omeprazole.
stop: Stop if diarrhoea is bad or tummy pain continues
If your eyes turn yellow or urine gets dark, stop and see a doctor (liver)
If your heart pounds and the pulse is irregular, stop and see a doctor
tips: Take it at the time written on the bag (before or after meals).
If your stomach burns, an acid medicine (famotidine) is the right one, not this — they're different medicines.

faq.q: How is it different from digestive enzymes?
faq.a: Digestive enzymes break down food; mosapride gets the stomach moving. If you feel bloated and food doesn't seem to go down, this is the one.

faq.q: Can I buy it at a pharmacy?
faq.a: No, it's a prescription medicine. If it's in your bag, take it as prescribed; if not, use pharmacy digestive enzymes or simethicone.

almagate.tagline: An antacid that puts out heartburn right now
almagate.lead: An antacid that neutralises stomach acid at once. It works within minutes but wears off in 1–2 hours. It doesn't block acid 'production' — it 'neutralises' acid that's already there — so there's no evidence it prevents anti-inflammatory stomach ulcers. If your stomach burns while taking anti-inflammatories, try famotidine; what has evidence for preventing ulcers is a prescription acid suppressant.
stop: If you've been taking it every day for more than 2 weeks, see a doctor
Stop if constipation gets bad
Black stools or vomiting blood: emergency department at once
tips: One sachet when it's urgent; if it keeps coming back, switch to famotidine or see a doctor.

faq.q: Can an antacid prevent ulcers from anti-inflammatories?
faq.a: No. It only neutralises acid that's already there and doesn't block its production, so there's no evidence for prevention. If your stomach burns while taking anti-inflammatories, try famotidine; what has evidence for preventing ulcers is a prescription acid suppressant.

faq.q: Can I take it with other medicines?
faq.a: Keep them 2 hours apart. It interferes with absorption. If you have kidney disease, aluminium and magnesium can build up, so avoid it.

loperamide.tagline: Stops diarrhoea — never with fever or bloody stools
loperamide.lead: It slows the bowel to stop diarrhoea. It's useful for watery diarrhoea before travel or an important day, but **with bacterial gastroenteritis — fever, or blood or mucus in the stool — it effectively traps the bacteria, so you mustn't take it**. Don't use it for more than two days; replacing fluids and electrolytes comes first.
for: Sudden watery diarrhoea (without fever or blood)
stop: New fever or bloody stools
Your tummy swells tight and you can't pass wind
tips: Most diarrhoea gets better by itself within 2–3 days. Use the medicine only when you 'really must stop it'.
Water + electrolytes (a sports drink diluted half with water, or oral rehydration solution) are the real treatment.

faq.q: I have diarrhoea with a fever — can I take it?
faq.a: No. With bacterial gastroenteritis — fever, blood or mucus — it effectively traps the bacteria, so you mustn't take it. Replacing fluids and electrolytes comes first; see a doctor.

faq.q: For how many days can I take it?
faq.a: Up to 2 days, and no more than 8 mg (4 capsules) a day. Most diarrhoea gets better by itself within 2–3 days, so use it only when you really must stop it. Don't buy it at a pharmacy for children under 9 — the leaflet contraindicates it under 24 months, and above that the child's dose is set by a doctor.

loperamide.children: Under 9, there's no approved dose, so talk to a doctor. Age 9–12: 2 mg at a time, up to 6 mg a day.

dimenhydrinate.tagline: A motion sickness medicine taken 30 minutes–1 hour before travel — expect drowsiness
dimenhydrinate.lead: A 2022 pooled analysis: first-generation antihistamines (dimenhydrinate, cinnarizine) prevented motion sickness in real travel. Of 100 people who took them, 40 had no motion sickness at all, versus 25 with placebo (3 trials, 240 people). But drowsiness was more common, 66 in 100 versus 44 with placebo. Take it 30 minutes to 1 hour before you leave, and drivers shouldn't take it.
stop: Don't take it for more than a week — it slows recovery
Stop if you become confused or can't pass urine
If dizziness comes with weakness in an arm or leg on one side or slurred speech, call 119 at once
tips: For seasickness or long trips, a scopolamine patch; for short car trips, this medicine.

faq.q: Can I take it after the motion sickness starts?
faq.a: That's too late. Take it 30 minutes to 1 hour before you leave. If it's already started, opening a window, lying down or closing your eyes helps more.

faq.q: Can drivers take it?
faq.a: No. In the 2022 pooled analysis it prevented motion sickness but caused more drowsiness. Avoid it with glaucoma or an enlarged prostate, and over 65 it can cause dry mouth, constipation and urine retention.

clotrimazole.tagline: The basic antifungal cream for athlete's foot, jock itch and candida
clotrimazole.lead: An azole that stops fungi from building their cell membrane. It's used not only for athlete's foot but also for jock itch in the groin, pityriasis versicolor on the body and candida skin rashes. In pooled analyses it clearly heals better than placebo (70% fewer failures), but it's **a little less effective than allylamines such as terbinafine and has to be applied for longer (2–4 weeks)**.
stop: If the area swells badly or blisters, stop and talk to a pharmacist or doctor
If nothing changes after four weeks, it may not be a fungal infection — get it checked
If the foot turns red and swollen with a fever, bacteria have joined in and a cream won't be enough
tips: If the skin between the toes is soggy, a powder or solution may be easier than a cream.
Change socks every day, and alternate shoes so each pair dries for a day.

faq.q: How is it different from terbinafine?
faq.a: Both kill fungi, but **terbinafine (an allylamine) works a little better and for a shorter time** (pooled analysis: a third fewer failures). Clotrimazole, on the other hand, also covers candida, so it's often used in the groin and skin folds.

clotrimazole.children: Can be used over age 2. At age 2 or under, or in the nappy area, follow a doctor's advice.

loxoprofen.tagline: Patches at the pharmacy, tablets on prescription — same ingredient, different category
loxoprofen.lead: An anti-inflammatory painkiller often prescribed in Korea. It's a prodrug that turns into its active form inside the body, so it's described as irritating the stomach less when absorbed, but it wasn't included in the large stomach and heart comparison data. **The tablets are prescription-only, while patches and poultices are sold at pharmacies** in Korea, and in a study of arm and leg injuries the patch worked as well as the tablets with half the side effects.
sideEffects: Rarely, stomach bleeding or reduced kidney function
Hives or an asthma attack (in people sensitive to anti-inflammatories)
stop: If your stomach burns or stools turn black, stop at once and see a doctor
If you pass less urine and get swelling, stop and see a doctor
If hives or breathlessness come on, stop immediately
tips: For pain in one spot, a patch works as well as tablets with half the side effects (comparison trial).

faq.q: Which is better, tablets or a patch?
faq.a: In a study of arm and leg injuries, the patch worked as well as the tablets with half the side effects. For pain in one area, try the patch first. In Korea patches are sold at pharmacies and tablets need a prescription.

faq.q: I heard it's gentler on the stomach?
faq.a: Because it turns into its active form inside the body, it's described as irritating the stomach less when absorbed, but that hasn't been proven in human trials. It isn't in the two large Western ranking studies, and in a Japanese case-control study (2006) the risk of stomach bleeding was similar to other anti-inflammatories (5.9 times that of people not taking it, versus 6.1 for other anti-inflammatories). In a 2-week endoscopy trial (2013), 28 in 100 developed stomach or duodenal ulcers (3 with placebo), the same level as ordinary anti-inflammatories. If you've had a stomach ulcer, avoid it.

erdosteine.tagline: Thins phlegm — two or three times a day
erdosteine.lead: A medicine that thins phlegm so it's easier to cough up. It does the same job as acetylcysteine, and its approved directions are **two or three times a day** (acetylcysteine is three times a day). **About 100 non-prescription products** are registered with Korea's drug regulator, so you can buy it straight from a Korean pharmacy. It doesn't suppress coughing — it works because **less phlegm means less phlegmy cough**.
for: Sticky phlegm that won't come up
sideEffects: Rarely, headache or a change in taste
stop: If there's blood in the phlegm, see a doctor at once
If the phlegm is unchanged after 10 days, don't take more — see a doctor
If your eyes turn yellow or urine gets dark, stop and see a doctor (liver)
If hives or breathlessness come on, stop immediately
tips: Acetylcysteine is three times a day, while this medicine's approved directions are two or three times a day — easier if you tend to forget doses.
Phlegm medicines are 'thinning medicines'. If a dry cough keeps you awake at night, you need a different medicine.

faq.q: How is it different from acetylcysteine?
faq.a: They do the same job — they thin phlegm. This medicine's approved directions are **two or three times a day**, and acetylcysteine is three times a day. There's no reason to take both together.

faq.q: For how many days can I take it?
faq.a: For a cough that started suddenly, the approved label says **not more than 10 days in a row**. If the phlegm is still the same by then, the answer isn't to change the medicine — **the cause needs to be checked**.

erdosteine.children: The pharmacy capsules are approved for adult doses only. Before giving it to a child, talk to a pharmacist or doctor.

omeprazole.tagline: The strongest acid suppressant — prescription-only in Korea
omeprazole.lead: It blocks the stomach's acid pump itself, so it's the strongest acid suppressant. It's the class with the strongest evidence for preventing anti-inflammatory stomach ulcers (pooled analysis: 60% fewer ulcers), and the stomach protector added to clinic anti-inflammatory prescriptions is usually this medicine. The US, UK and Japan sell a low dose at pharmacies, but **in Korea it's still prescription-only**, so Korean pharmacies only sell the weaker famotidine. Whether to take it longer than 8 weeks is a doctor's decision.
sideEffects: With long use, low vitamin B12 or magnesium
With long use, bowel infection (Clostridium) and weaker bones become slightly more common
stop: If you get watery diarrhoea with a fever, stop and see a doctor (bowel infection)
Tell your doctor if your hands and feet tingle and you feel weak — long use lowers vitamin B12 and magnesium
If swallowing is hard or you're losing weight, don't take more — get tested
If you've been taking it for more than 8 weeks, check again whether you still need it
tips: If you've had a stomach ulcer and need anti-inflammatories for a long time, it's safer to see a doctor for a prescription of 'celecoxib + a strong acid suppressant' than to use a pharmacy combination.

faq.q: Can I buy it at a pharmacy?
faq.a: In Korea it's still prescription-only, although the US, UK and Japan sell a low dose at pharmacies. Korean pharmacies sell the weaker famotidine.

faq.q: Can I take it for a long time?
faq.a: Beyond 8 weeks it needs a doctor's judgement. Long use carries risks of low vitamin B12 and magnesium, fractures and bowel infection, so over 65 it's reassessed after 8 weeks.

alginate.tagline: A medicine that floats a 'raft' on top of the stomach to block reflux
alginate.lead: When it meets stomach acid it forms a gel layer that floats on top of the stomach contents and physically stops acid from rising into the gullet. It suits reflux after meals and before lying down especially well, and it also contains an antacid.
stop: If swallowing is hard or you're losing weight, don't take more — see a doctor
If it hasn't helped after 7 days, see a doctor
Black stools or vomiting blood: emergency department at once
tips: If reflux is the main symptom, alginate suits better than an antacid; for pain on an empty stomach, an antacid.
Not lying down right after eating and finishing meals 3 hours before bed matter more than the medicine.

faq.q: How is it different from an antacid?
faq.a: When it meets stomach acid it forms a gel layer (a raft) that floats on top of the stomach contents and physically stops acid from rising into the gullet. If reflux is the main symptom, alginate; for pain on an empty stomach, an antacid.

faq.q: I have heart or kidney problems — is it OK?
faq.a: It contains sodium, so be careful with heart failure, a low-salt diet or kidney disease. Not lying down right after eating and finishing meals 3 hours before bed matter more than the medicine.

smectite.tagline: An anti-diarrhoeal that soaks up toxins and water — not for children, pregnancy or breastfeeding
smectite.lead: Its clay ingredient soaks up toxins and water in the bowel to reduce diarrhoea. Unlike loperamide it doesn't stop the bowel moving, so it can be used for infectious diarrhoea, but Korea's drug regulator restricted its use over concerns about lead exposure, so **the current label approves it for adults only, and it isn't taken by children or during pregnancy or breastfeeding**.
stop: If diarrhoea lasts more than two days or there's fever or blood in the stool, stop and see a doctor
If you couldn't keep other medicines 2 hours apart, those medicines may work less well
tips: Mix it well in water. Replacing fluids is still a must, separately.

faq.q: Can I give it to my child?
faq.a: No. The current label approves it for adults only, and it isn't taken by children or during pregnancy or breastfeeding (restricted by Korea's drug regulator over lead exposure concerns). For a child's diarrhoea, water and electrolytes come first — see a doctor.

faq.q: What if I take it with other medicines?
faq.a: Keep them 2 hours apart. As an absorbent, it blocks other medicines from being absorbed. Replacing fluids is still a must, separately.

smectite.children: Not used in children (the current label contraindicates it).

tiropramide.tagline: An antispasmodic used by clinics for cramping pain
tiropramide.lead: A prescription antispasmodic for **pain caused by hollow tubes squeezing**, such as the bowel, bile ducts and urinary tract. It doesn't work by blocking nerves; it **acts directly on the muscle** to relax it, so dry mouth, glare sensitivity and trouble passing urine — common with anticholinergics — are less frequent (though they can rarely happen). In clinics it's sometimes used alongside a painkiller for **the squeezing pain of cystitis**, kidney-stone colic or bile-duct spasm.
stop: If a rash or itching spreads, stop and see a doctor
If you have a fever and pain in your side, see a doctor at once
tips: It **works differently from a painkiller (acetaminophen), so they can be used together.** Ask at your visit whether you need both.
A warm water bottle on the lower tummy makes things much more comfortable alongside the medicine.

faq.q: I have cystitis and only got a painkiller. Can I ask for this medicine?
faq.a: **Yes, you can ask.** Just say: 'It hurts like squeezing when I pass urine — could you also give me an antispasmodic?' Cystitis pain is a spasm of the bladder muscle, so an antispasmodic often helps, and it works differently from a painkiller so they can be used together. But **the antibiotic comes first**; the antispasmodic is an add-on.

tiropramide.children: Data in children are limited, so a doctor needs to decide.

scopolamine.tagline: Behind the ear 4 hours before you leave — the children's version is prescription-only
scopolamine.lead: Stuck behind the ear, it prevents motion sickness for 3 days. It has to go on **at least 4 hours before you leave** to work, and if you touch your eyes without washing your hands after applying it, your pupils widen and your vision blurs. In Korea the children's patch (age 8–15) is prescription-only, and it's not used at age 7 or under, in pregnancy, or with glaucoma or an enlarged prostate.
stop: Confusion or hallucinations
Badly blurred vision
tips: For short trips, a motion sickness tablet (dimenhydrinate) is simpler.
After wearing patches for several days, removing them can bring dizziness, nausea and headache for a few days (approved label).

faq.q: Can I put it on right before I leave?
faq.a: It needs to go on at least 4 hours before to work. One patch lasts 3 days.

faq.q: My vision went dim after putting it on.
faq.a: Touching your eyes with the hand that applied it widens the pupils and blurs your vision. Wash your hands after applying it. It's not used at age 7 or under, in pregnancy, or with glaucoma or an enlarged prostate, and over 65 there's a risk of confusion and hallucinations.

scopolamine.children: Not at age 7 or under; age 8–15 on prescription.

chlorhexidine.tagline: An antiseptic mouthwash that cuts mouth bacteria — it won't ease pain
chlorhexidine.lead: An antiseptic mouthwash that reduces bacteria in the mouth. It's used for gum inflammation, care after a tooth extraction and stopping mouth ulcers from getting infected. But **it doesn't directly reduce pain** — for pain you need a benzydamine mouthwash (pharmacy) or a gel you apply. Long use stains the teeth, so use it **for 2 weeks or less**.
stop: If the inside of your mouth peels, swells or hurts, stop and get advice
**Don't go beyond 2 weeks** — the teeth stain brown and taste dulls
Keep it 30 minutes apart from toothpaste. Used straight after, they cancel each other out
tips: It doesn't replace brushing. It's an add-on used 30 minutes after brushing your teeth.

faq.q: Is chlorhexidine alone enough for a mouth ulcer?
faq.a: It isn't enough. Chlorhexidine is **an antiseptic that stops it getting infected**; it can't reduce the pain. For pain, use a gel you apply (such as a triamcinolone oral paste) or a benzydamine mouthwash alongside it to feel comfortable. In Korea both are sold at pharmacies.

chlorhexidine.children: Check the child is old enough not to swallow it; for young children, follow a doctor's or dentist's advice.

artificial-tears.tagline: Single-use vials: open and use at once; bottles with preservative: up to 4 times a day
artificial-tears.lead: They top up the tear film to ease dryness and a gritty feeling. In Korea carboxymethylcellulose types are sold at pharmacies, while hyaluronic acid types are mostly prescription (covered by insurance). Don't reuse single-use vials once opened, and bottled products with preservative are meant for up to 4 times a day.
stop: If the eye hurts, turns red and vision blurs, see an eye doctor at once
If nothing changes after a month of use, the cause needs finding
tips: If you need them more than 4 times a day, switch to preservative-free single-use vials.
If redness is the main symptom, get the cause checked instead of using 'drops that take the red out'.

faq.q: How many times a day?
faq.a: Bottled products with preservative up to 4 times a day; if more often, preservative-free single-use vials. Don't reuse single-use vials once opened.

faq.q: Can I also use drops that take the red out?
faq.a: Redness relievers (vasoconstrictors) cause rebound redness if used for 3 days or more. If redness is the main symptom, get the cause checked.

salicylic-corn.tagline: Softens hard skin so it peels off — only on the corn itself
salicylic-corn.lead:
It's **a medicine that softens hardened skin so it peels off**. In a trial that split 202 people into groups, those using salicylic acid plasters saw **34 in 100 corns disappear completely** in three months, versus 21 with scalpel paring.

But **if you have diabetes or poor circulation in your feet, talk to a doctor before using it** (the leaflet says not to use it) — if healthy skin gets soggy too, it can become a wound that heals poorly. **First change your shoes to reduce the pressure.**
for: Warts (plaster products — if unsure, get it checked by a dermatologist first)
sideEffects: Surrounding skin turns white and soggy and stings
stop: If it turns red and swollen with warmth or pus, stop at once and see a doctor
If the surrounding skin peels and hurts, take a few days off
If nothing changes after several weeks, it may be a wart — get it checked by a dermatologist
tips: After a bath, when the skin is soft, rubbing gently with a pumice stone or file helps the plaster work better.
A doughnut-shaped pad that moves pressure away makes it hurt less even without medicine.

faq.q: Wouldn't cutting it out heal faster?
faq.a: In the trial, **more corns disappeared with the plasters.** Time until it came back was longer in the first analysis, but a 1-year follow-up re-analysis found no clear difference. Cutting it out at home with a knife or nail clippers can cause a wound that gets infected.

salicylic-corn.children: The liquid isn't used under age 7. Don't put plasters on babies under 2 either, and children should use them with a parent watching.

felbinac.tagline: Not just ketoprofen — another type of pharmacy anti-inflammatory patch
felbinac.lead: An anti-inflammatory you stick on. It does the same job as a ketoprofen patch but **has a different ingredient**, so it's worth switching to if a ketoprofen patch made your skin itch or burn. **23 products** are registered as pharmacy products with Korea's drug regulator. Another advantage: unlike ketoprofen, you don't have to keep the patch area out of sunlight after removing it.
stop: If blisters form, don't use that ingredient again
If the area stays itchy and red, remove it, rest a day, then switch to a different ingredient
If nothing changes after five or six days, stop and get advice
tips: It's the first alternative worth suggesting to people whose skin itched with a ketoprofen patch.
On hairy areas, trimming a little before applying makes removal less painful.

faq.q: How is it different from a ketoprofen patch?
faq.a: They do the same job. But **the ingredient is different, so it feels different on the skin.** And with ketoprofen you must keep the area out of sunlight for up to 2 weeks after removing it, while felbinac has no such restriction.

felbinac.children: The age limit differs by product. Check the box.

topical-steroid.tagline: The surest medicine for itching and eczema — short, for the set period only
topical-steroid.lead: A medicine that calms skin inflammation directly. For eczema and dermatitis, insect bites and itching it works **the fastest and most reliably**. Many people avoid anything called a steroid, but **what pharmacies sell is the weakest level**, so if you use it only for the set period, worrying side effects are rare — in a pooled analysis, skin thinning happened in **about 1 in 100 people**, and mostly with much stronger medicines. Far more often, people apply too little out of fear, scratch, and the rash spreads. Just remember that **applying it on infections such as fungus or herpes makes them worse**, so that's the one thing to tell apart.
sideEffects: With long use, thinner skin or visible small blood vessels
stop: If nothing changes after a week or it spreads further, stop and see a doctor
If the skin gets thin and small blood vessels show through, stop and get advice
If it oozes and yellow crusts form, fungus or bacteria have joined in and a steroid alone won't do
tips: Apply plenty of moisturiser first, then put the steroid only on the itchy areas.
Once or twice a day is often enough. Applying it before bed is easiest to keep up.
If you stop the day it seems better, it comes back. Keep applying for a day or two after it settles, then stop.

faq.q: I'm scared because it's a steroid.
faq.a: Pooling 8,443 people, **skin thinning happened in about 1 in 100**, and mostly in people using much stronger medicines. What pharmacies sell is the weakest level, based on one week, so it's on the safer side. Far more often, people apply too little out of fear, scratch, and the rash spreads.

faq.q: How many times a day should I apply it?
faq.a: The approved directions are **1–3 times a day depending on the product**. In a pooled analysis with strong steroids, applying once a day and twice a day helped the same number of people, so **once or twice a day is often enough.** It's not a medicine that works better the more often you apply it — it's one you **start on time, apply enough of, and stop on time**.

faq.q: Can I put it on athlete's foot?
faq.a: **No.** The itch eases for a while, but the fungus spreads further and you suffer much longer later. If it itches between your toes, check with an athlete's foot medicine first.

faq.q: Can I stop as soon as it seems better?
faq.a: It's better to **keep applying for a day or two** after it settles, then stop. For spots that keep coming back, there's research that **applying it only at weekends after it settles** greatly reduces flare-ups (pooled analysis: from 58 in 100 having a flare-up to 25). But discuss this method with a doctor first.

topical-steroid.children: For children, a weaker one for a shorter time. In the nappy area, follow a doctor's advice.

albendazole.tagline: For pinworm, 'once more after 7 days' — and the whole family together
albendazole.lead: A medicine that clears parasites such as roundworm, pinworm, hookworm and whipworm. It's sold at pharmacies in Korea, and **one tablet is often enough.** But **with pinworm, eggs survive and hatch again, so take another dose after 7 days**, and as a rule **the whole family takes it together** — if only one person takes it, it spreads back quickly.
sideEffects: Stomach upset, tummy pain or diarrhoea
Uncommonly, hepatitis — newly added to the label in 2026
stop: If your eyes turn yellow, urine gets dark or you feel drained for no reason, stop and see a doctor (hepatitis)
If sores appear in your mouth and eyes while blisters or red spots spread on your skin, stop at once and go to the emergency department
If you have a fever and sore throat and feel drained, see a doctor (low white blood cells)
If hives or breathlessness come on, stop immediately
tips: Many people do 'whole-family deworming' every spring and autumn, but **if there are no symptoms, you don't need to take it regularly.** Infection rates in Korea are low nowadays.
If a child scratches their bottom at night and sleeps badly, it may be pinworm — that's when to use this medicine.

faq.q: Do I have to take it every year?
faq.a: If there are no symptoms, **you don't need to take it regularly.** Unlike in the past, parasite infections in Korea have fallen a lot. Take it **when pinworm is suspected**, for example a child scratching their bottom at night. If you often eat raw freshwater fish, **this medicine won't cure liver flukes** — have a stool test at a public health centre or hospital and get the right medicine (prescription).

faq.q: Why take it again after 7 days?
faq.a: With pinworm, **the medicine doesn't work well on the eggs.** Even after the first dose kills the adult worms, the remaining eggs hatch about 7 days later. You need another dose then to finish. Korea's disease control agency, allowing for reinfection, advises taking it **3 or more times, 20 days apart** (the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention: once more after 2 weeks). Decide with a pharmacist or doctor how many more doses to take.

faq.q: Does the whole family need to take it?
faq.a: With pinworm, **yes.** The eggs spread on hands, underwear and bedding, so people living together are usually infected too. If only one person takes it, it comes back quickly. **Korea's disease control agency also says the whole family of an infected person should be treated at the same time** (for babies under 2, ask a doctor first).

albendazole.children: From age 2 (24 months), the same 1 tablet (400 mg) as adults. If it's hard to swallow, it can be chewed or taken with water.

bisphosphonate.tagline: First-line treatment for osteoporosis — it only works if you take it the right way
bisphosphonate.lead: A prescription medicine that slows bone breakdown and **actually reduces fractures**. It's the backbone of osteoporosis treatment. But it's very hard to absorb, so **if you don't follow how to take it, it hardly works at all**, and it can damage the gullet. That's why with this medicine, half of it is not 'what you take' but **'how you take it'**. And **before dental treatment, you must tell the dentist you're taking it**.
for: Bone loss from taking steroids for a long time
stop: If swallowing hurts or the middle of your chest burns, stop and see a doctor
If a tooth-extraction site hasn't healed after several weeks, see a doctor
tips: **Pick a day of the week.** Marking a calendar or setting a phone alarm helps you not forget. Once-a-week medicines are easy to forget.
Taking it after you get up and go to the toilet, before breakfast, is easiest to keep up.
Always use plenty of **plain water**. Bottled or filtered water is fine, but mineral water is better avoided.
If you plan dental work, it's best to **get your teeth sorted before starting the medicine**.

faq.q: Once I start, do I take it for life?
faq.a: No. Usually after **3–5 years** your bone density and fracture risk are checked again to decide whether to continue or take a break (drug holiday). Don't stop on your own; at a visit, ask 'How much longer should I take it?'

faq.q: Taking it is such a hassle — is there an injection?
faq.a: Yes. There's an injection under the skin every 6 months and a drip into a vein once a year. If it's hard to follow the instructions or your stomach burns too much, **ask about the injection forms at your visit.**

faq.q: I heard jawbone damage is frightening.
faq.a: At osteoporosis doses it's **very rare.** It's mainly reported at the high doses used for cancer treatment. And prevention is clear — **tell your dentist you're taking it before an extraction or implant**, and look after your gums day to day. If fear stops you treating osteoporosis, the risk of fracture is far greater.

bisphosphonate.children: Used in children only in special cases.
